newsitem.title: GERMANY: German house rejects SPD motion for tax debate.
newsitem.headline: German house rejects SPD motion for tax debate.

text.p: The lower house of the German parliament on Friday rejected a call by opposition Social Democrats (SPD) for an immediate debate on the government's tax policies.
The opposition is alarmed that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition is considering raising the petroleum tax or delaying the planned cut in the solidarity surcharge.
Coalition leaders interrupted an internal discussion to take part in the lower house vote. They were expected to continue their talks until midday.
Coalition officials have said they expect the tax policy to be clarified today, ahead of a Christian Democrat (CDU) party congress next week.

A decision this week to allow a wealth tax to lapse at year end and to increase government child allowance at the beginning of 1997 has set the government scrambling to fill a 1997 spending gap estimated at 10 to 11 billion marks.
